minutes.headline: Committee reorganized with four members; reviewed the special town meeting warrant, with public hearing set for the 24th.
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee, down to four members after two resignations, reorganized by roll call vote, with the former vice chair becoming chair. It then walked through the draft special town meeting warrant article by article with the interim town manager, including late bills, Chapter 70 money, revolving funds, a building study and large salary plan changes. Questions were deferred to the October 24 hearing; no recommendations were voted.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee, down to four members after two resignations, reorganized by roll call vote with all four voting aye.
The committee walked through the draft special town meeting warrant article by article with the interim town manager, including a late bill, Chapter 70 money and revolving funds.
No recommendations were voted; the October 24 meeting will serve as the presentation and public hearing, with recommendations deferred in the booklet by an insert sheet.
The assessor is to be invited to the hearing to explain Article 11, and the town manager is to draft definitions of financial terms for the warrant booklet.
The committee decided to keep its next meeting on October 24 rather than meet next week.

why_it_matters: The warrant articles covered a transfer from overlay surplus, additional state school aid, revolving fund spending limits and a borrowing for Marshall Park, so they bear on what residents will be asked to vote on at special town meeting.
The Finance Committee has not yet taken a position on any article, so the October 24 hearing is the first point where residents can hear its questions answered before recommendations are printed.
watch_next: October 24 presentation and public hearing on the special town meeting warrant, with the assessor expected to explain Article 11.
The warrant booklet, with financial term definitions due from the town manager by Tuesday and recommendations deferred to an insert sheet.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the officer slate, the $4,180 overlay transfer, the $225,000 overlay figure, the four members and the Chapter 70 balance (once the captions are corrected). Where they differ, our recording has several spoken figures and follow-ups that the official minutes leave out, and the official minutes have housekeeping items we missed. The one to check first is who was to do what on the Council on Aging full-year leave or cost, and Carter's title (interim town manager versus Finance Director).
